# The code

> A guided tour of all nine packages: what each owns, and where to look when something breaks.

---

Nine packages. Their arrangement is not incidental — the dependency direction is the architecture,
and most bad ideas in this codebase announce themselves as a need to import upward.

## The dependency direction

```
@faravahar/girih-core  (kernel — depends on nothing)
↑ depended on by ↑
@faravahar/girih-tokens  (token pipeline)  +  @faravahar/girih-core
↑
@faravahar/girih-generator-css  (tokens → CSS)  ·  @faravahar/girih-spec  (contracts)
↑
@faravahar/girih-generator-react  (IR → React (core + spec))
↑
@faravahar/girih  (the only package allowed to depend on all of them)
standalone:
@faravahar/girih-react-runtime  (react is a peer dep)  create-girih  (zero workspace deps)  @faravahar/girih-figma  (phase-2 stub)
```

> **▶ The dependency direction** — interactive
>
> Hover a package to see what it may — and may not — import. Open [the interactive version](../06-the-code.html) in a browser to use it.

> **🔵 Rule — If a fix seems to need an upward import, it belongs somewhere else**
>
> Every time this rule feels inconvenient, the logic wants to move down rather than the dependency
> move up. Something both `tokens` and `spec` need goes in
> `core`. Something `tokens` needs from `spec` is almost certainly
> a sign the responsibility is on the wrong side of the line.
>
> Nothing enforces this mechanically — no lint rule, no dependency-cruiser config. It is a review
> responsibility, which is why it is stated in `CLAUDE.md` and here.

> **🟢 In plain words**
>
> Picture a pyramid. `core` is the bottom block and holds nothing up but itself.
> Each layer may rest on the ones below it and never on the ones above. The CLI sits on top, which
> is why it can see everything — and why nothing may depend on the CLI.

## @faravahar/girih-core — the shared kernel

Small on purpose. Four files, and every one exists so that other packages cannot disagree with
each other.

| File | Exports | Why it is here and not elsewhere |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `config.ts` | `loadConfig`, `defineConfig`, `ResolvedConfig`, `CONFIG_FILENAMES` | Everything needs the workspace shape; jiti loads the TS config at runtime |
| `diagnostics.ts` | `Diagnostic`, `DiagnosticBag`, `formatDiagnostic` | One reporting vocabulary, so the CLI can render any package's problems identically |
| `files.ts` | `emittedFile`, `writeEmittedFiles`, `verifyEmittedFiles` | One hashing and writing path — drift detection and publish diffing both depend on the hash being computed the same way everywhere |
| `naming.ts` | `cssVarName` | Emitted `tokens.css`, `tokens.d.ts` and `components.css` must agree on variable names or the output silently breaks |

**packages/girih-core/src/files.ts  [You write this]**

```ts
export function emittedFile(path: string, contents: string): EmittedFile {
  return { path, contents, hash: createHash('sha256').update(contents).digest('hex') };
}

/** Paths whose on-disk contents differ from the given files — the CI staleness gate. */
export async function verifyEmittedFiles(root: string, files: EmittedFile[]): Promise<string[]> {
  const stale: string[] = [];
  for (const file of files) {
    const onDisk = await readFile(join(root, file.path), 'utf8').catch(() => null);
    if (onDisk !== file.contents) stale.push(file.path);
  }
  return stale;
}
```

Twelve lines carrying four features: drift detection, the `--check` CI gate, orphan
cleanup, and bake-time staleness refusal. Worth reading before you write anything that emits a
file.

## @faravahar/girih-tokens — the pipeline

| File | Owns | Start here when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `engine.ts` | `buildTokenGraphs()` — orchestrates everything; `inferTier()` | You want the overall flow, or tier inference is wrong |
| `parse.ts` | DTCG reading, `$type` inheritance | A token file is misread or a type is not inherited |
| `merge.ts` | `mergeTokenFiles()`, `applyBrandOverlay()`, `toNestedDtcg()` | An overlay does the wrong thing, or the override-only rule misfires |
| `resolve.ts` | `resolveTokenSet()` — aliases, cycles, poison propagation | A value resolves wrongly, or a cycle report is confusing |
| `validate.ts` | `validateTierDirection()`, `validateBrandParity()` | A tier or parity error looks wrong |

`resolve.ts` is the densest file in the repository and the one most worth reading in
full. Three algorithms share it, and the ordering between them is load-bearing:

1. **Unknown-reference detection**, deduped so a value containing  `{missing}` twice reports once, with a "did you mean" search over the real token set.
2. **Cycle detection** — an iterative depth-first search with grey/black colouring,  reporting each cycle once with its _full_ chain. Iterative rather than recursive so a  pathological alias graph cannot blow the stack.
3. **Poison propagation** — a reverse-graph walk marking everything that can reach a  broken token as unresolvable, while reporting only the root cause.

> **🟡 Watch out — Why substitution is delegated to style-dictionary**
>
> girih finds and validates references itself but hands the final string substitution to
> `style-dictionary`'s `resolveReferences`. That is deliberate: alias
> semantics for edge cases — a reference embedded mid-string, composite values, DTCG's
> `usesDtcg` mode — should match what the rest of the token ecosystem does, rather than
> being girih's private interpretation. Composite values (shadow, typography) are walked manually so
> references _inside_ objects and arrays resolve too.

## @faravahar/girih-generator-css

Three files, and one function inside them matters more than the rest.

**packages/girih-generator-css/src/generate.ts  [You write this]**

```ts
/** The given paths plus every token that (transitively) references one of them. */
function dependentsClosure(roots: string[], graph: ResolvedTokenGraph): Set<string> {
  const closure = new Set(roots);
  if (closure.size === 0) return closure;

  const dependents = new Map<string, string[]>();
  for (const token of graph.tokens.values()) {
    for (const ref of token.references) {
      if (!dependents.has(ref)) dependents.set(ref, []);
      dependents.get(ref)!.push(token.path);
    }
  }

  const queue = [...closure];
  while (queue.length > 0) {
    const current = queue.pop()!;
    for (const dependent of dependents.get(current) ?? []) {
      if (!closure.has(dependent)) { closure.add(dependent); queue.push(dependent); }
    }
  }
  return closure;
}
```

Build the reverse reference graph, then breadth-first from the overridden paths. That set is what
each brand block must re-declare, and [chapter 04](04-tokens.md#closure) explains why
omitting it produces a partial, plausible-looking failure.

Two guards in the same file are worth knowing because they turn silent breakage into build errors:

- `detectVarNameCollisions()` — two token paths mapping to one CSS variable name is a  silent last-one-wins in CSS. `GIRIH3003`, hard error.
- `detectUnserializableValues()` — scans the emitted CSS for  `[object Object]`, which is what a composite value looks like when no transform could  flatten it. `GIRIH3002`.

The package also emits `tokens.d.ts`: a `TokenPath` string-literal union of
every real token path. That is what makes token references in contracts type-checked rather than
merely string-shaped.

## @faravahar/girih-spec

| File | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `define.ts` | `defineSpec()`, `isSpec()`, the `SPEC_BRAND` marker |
| `types.ts` | The contract shape — the most useful file to read first |
| `ir.ts` | `specToIR()` — canonicalisation |
| `load.ts` | `loadSpecs()`, `loadComponentIRs()` — jiti-based TS import |
| `validate.ts` | `validateSpecs()`, `validateExtensions()` — 31 diagnostics |
| `extensions.ts` | `defineVariant()`, `loadExtensions()`, `componentNamespace()` |

`SPEC_BRAND` and `EXTENSION_BRAND` are runtime markers stamped by
`defineSpec`/`defineVariant`. They exist because contracts are loaded from
arbitrary user TypeScript, and girih needs to distinguish "a contract" from "some object someone
default-exported" without trusting the type system across a runtime boundary.

## @faravahar/girih-generator-react

| File | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `generate.ts` | `generateReact()`, `renderComponentSource()`, the package + index emission |
| `css.ts` | `renderComponentCss()`, `renderExtensionCss()`, state selectors, element-class tables |
| `templates/registry.ts` | `TEMPLATE_REGISTRY` — capabilities and versions per template |
| `templates/element.ts` | The general single-element template (Button, Badge, Card, Input) |
| `templates/checkbox.ts` | Styled native input — a real element with a real indicator |
| `templates/dialog.ts` | Base UI behind an adapter — focus trap, scroll lock, ARIA |

`TEMPLATE_REGISTRY` is consulted from two places that are easy to miss:
contract validation, so an unimplementable state is a build error rather than a missing CSS rule;
and ejection, which records the template version so `girih forks` can report a fork
whose template has since moved.

## @faravahar/girih

| File | Owns |
| --- | --- |
| `cli.ts` | Every command, plus `composeReact()` — the single source of truth for what gets written |
| `build.ts` | `buildPackage()`, `addJsExtensions()`, `emitDeclarations()` |
| `manifest.ts` | `detectDrift()`, `planManifestUpdate()`, read/write manifest |
| `lock.ts` | `readLock()`, `writeLock()` — ejections and the published baseline |
| `semver.ts` | `computeSignature()`, `diffSignatures()`, `applyBump()` |
| `scaffold.ts` | `scaffoldWorkspace()` — shared by `init` and `create-girih` |
| `output.ts` | `printDiagnostics()`, `table()` — terminal rendering |

> **🟡 Watch out — addJsExtensions() looks like a hack and is not**
>
> TypeScript emits `import { Button } from './Button'` with no file extension. Under
> Node's ESM resolution that is a runtime error, and which consumer setups break depends on their
> `moduleResolution` setting — so it fails for some users and not others, which is the
> worst kind of packaging bug.
>
> `addJsExtensions()` rewrites relative specifiers to include `.js` in the
> built output, which is why the packed tarball resolves correctly under every consumer
> configuration. `e2e/test/consumer.test.ts` is what proves it: it packs a real tarball,
> installs it into a scratch consumer, and server-renders every component.

## @faravahar/girih-react-runtime

One file, three exports, and `react` is a _peer_ dependency — never a real one,
or a consumer could end up with two Reacts.

| Export | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `BrandProvider` | Renders a wrapper carrying `data-brand`, and publishes the brand on a context |
| `useBrand` | Reads the current brand — for the rare case where JS needs to know |
| `cx` | Class-name join. Deliberately tiny: no `clsx` dependency in generated output |

That is the entire runtime cost of girih's theming. Everything else is CSS resolving in the
browser.

## create-girih and @faravahar/girih-figma

`create-girih` has **zero workspace dependencies**, which is a constraint
rather than an oversight: it has to run via `npx` before anything is installed, so it
cannot import `@faravahar/girih`. It detects the package manager from the environment and
shells out.

`@faravahar/girih-figma` is a private phase-2 stub. It consumes `ComponentIR`, which is
the reason the IR exists as a target-neutral form at all. Do not grow it without being asked.

## Where to look when something breaks

| Symptom | Look at | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A token resolves to the wrong value | `tokens/src/resolve.ts` | `girih check --brand X` to see the resolved table |
| A brand override does not apply | `tokens/src/merge.ts` | Check `applyBrandOverlay()` recorded the path in `overriddenPaths` |
| Colour rebrands but radius does not | `generator-css/src/generate.ts` | `dependentsClosure()` — a missing closure member |
| A CSS variable has the wrong name | `core/src/naming.ts` | Every emitter must route through `cssVarName()` |
| A contract error seems wrong | `spec/src/validate.ts` | The tests enumerate intended failures with their codes |
| Emitted TSX is malformed | `generator-react/src/templates/` | Find the template for that `element` |
| A state has no CSS | `generator-react/src/css.ts` | `STATE_SELECTORS`, and whether the template claims the capability |
| `generate` refuses to run | `cli/src/manifest.ts` | `detectDrift()` — something was hand-edited |
| The wrong version is proposed | `cli/src/semver.ts` | `diffSignatures()` reasons; compare to `ds.lock` |
| The package fails to import downstream | `cli/src/build.ts` | `addJsExtensions()`, then the consumer e2e |

## The test layout

One root `vitest.config.ts`, no per-package config. It aliases five packages to their
source so unit tests run without a build:

**vitest.config.ts  [You write this]**

```ts
resolve: {
  // Tests run against source so packages don't need a build first.
  alias: {
    '@faravahar/girih-core': r('packages/girih-core/src/index.ts'),
    '@faravahar/girih-tokens': r('packages/girih-tokens/src/index.ts'),
    '@faravahar/girih-generator-css': r('packages/girih-generator-css/src/index.ts'),
    '@faravahar/girih-generator-react': r('packages/girih-generator-react/src/index.ts'),
    '@faravahar/girih-spec': r('packages/girih-spec/src/index.ts'),
  },
},
test: { include: ['packages/*/test/**/*.test.ts', 'e2e/test/**/*.test.ts'] },
```

> **🟡 Watch out — Two packages are deliberately NOT aliased**
>
> `@faravahar/girih` and `@faravahar/girih-react-runtime` are absent from that list. Anything
> exercising them runs against `dist/`, so `pnpm build` is required first.
> That is intentional for the CLI: the end-to-end tests should exercise the same compiled binary a
> user would run, not a source alias that might behave differently.

<details>
<summary><b>A known flake in the e2e suite — and its cause</b></summary>

`e2e/test/consumer.test.ts` intermittently fails with
`ENOENT … e2e/.tmp/consumer/app/smoke.mjs`. It passes when run alone.

The cause: `workspace.test.ts` removes the whole of `e2e/.tmp` in its
`afterAll`, while `consumer.test.ts` keeps its scratch directory under
`e2e/.tmp/consumer`. Vitest runs the two files in parallel, so one file's teardown can
delete a live sibling's working directory.

The fix, for whoever wants it, is to scope that teardown to `e2e/.tmp/e2e-ds` and
`e2e/.tmp/bad-brand` rather than the shared parent. It is recorded here so nobody
spends an afternoon debugging their own change.

</details>

Verification, smallest scope first: `pnpm vitest run packages/`, then
`pnpm typecheck`, then the example workspace's `girih check`, and only run
the consumer e2e when packaging changed.
